item.title: Meta’s Hyperion AI data center will sprawl to four times the size of Manhattan’s Central Park
item.description: Meta’s latest 1,400-acre land deal in Louisiana signals plans for a vast, multiphase AI campus unlike anything the U.S. has seen.

item.title: Scott Bessent’s ‘gotcha’ moment on Trump’s tariffs and inflation: He denies writing ‘tariffs are inflationary’ in letter to hedge fund investors
item.description: In 2024 Bessent wrote: “Tariffs are inflationary and would strengthen the dollar.” He denied this before the House Financial Services Committee.

item.title: Pinterest cracks down on dissent, fires engineers for an internal layoff tool as AI shake-ups keep employees on edge and in line
item.description: The incident shows how layoffs and AI investment have given employers more leverage over workers.

item.title: Scott Galloway predicts OpenAI could pull its IPO amid AI ‘vibe shift’ as investors ‘gag’ on Trump proximity, questionable revenue
item.description: “Sustainable advantage is really, really thin,” the NYU professor said of the potential $830 billion IPO.

item.title: Alphabet plans to double capex spending to a possible $185 billion—but it’s keeping CEO Sundar Pichai up at night
item.description: Alphabet revealed a staggering increase in infrastructure investments that will see it nearly double the $91.4 billion it spent last year, according to its fourth quarter earnings release.

item.title: IonQ, the biggest quantum computing company on the stock market, disputes short-seller claims it failed to disclose holes in its revenue
item.description: Short-seller Wolfpack Research says IonQ misled investors about cancelled government earmarks; it also points to suspicious insider stock sales.

item.title: S&P rings up 5th loss in 6 days as tech stocks drag index down, led by AMD’s 17.3% drop
item.description: More than twice as many stocks rose within the S&P 500 than fell, but sinking technology stocks weighed on the index for a second straight day.

item.title: Disney’s new D’Amaro-land: a dream team succession saga comes to life
item.description: Bob Iger was a returning general to Disney in 2022, but he built a roster of top lieutenants helping with his succession plan.

item.title: Having a college degree still matters for being one of the wealthier Americans, New York Fed says
item.description: The spending divide is visible in the past three years of data, the New York Fed says, and college degrees matter a lot.

item.title: Key Nevada legislator says lawmakers will push for independent audit of altered public record in Nevada OSHA’s Boring Company inspection
item.description: Because a forensic analysis conducted by the Governor’s Office was inconclusive, legislators are pushing for a third-party audit.
